# Near-triangle pentagons: two-cut union accounting and cap stability

This is an ordinary planar extraction theorem. It constructs ONE
enclosing triangle and controls its entire missing area, including
overlapping cuts and pieces extending almost halfway along a side.
It is not a mixed-integer theorem or a claim for arbitrary polygons.

Let Q be a full-dimensional convex pentagon, and suppose that for
some invertible affine map A,

    dist_H,infinity(AQ,T)<=1/1000000,
    T=conv(0,e_1,e_2).

Write D(Q) for its normalized ordinary maximum halfspace depth and
Gamma=4/9. Then there is a constructed full-dimensional triangle
S containing Q such that, with tau=1-|Q|/|S|,

    D(Q)-Gamma>=tau/180,
    tau/2<=dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_S)<=tau.                 (1)

Here mu_K is normalized uniform area measure and dist_cap is the
supremum of absolute probability differences over all closed
halfspaces. In particular

    inf_(triangles S') dist_cap(mu_Q,mu_S')
                         <=180[D(Q)-4/9].           (2)

No optimizing triangle or affine map is selected. The metric
hypothesis is the given existence of A. The proof works in that
frame and transports the constructed triangle back afterwards.

## 1. Three actual side lines selected near facet midpoints

Put delta=dist_H,infinity(Q,T)<=10^(-6). Convex Hausdorff
approximation gives

    T_inner={x,y>=delta, x+y<=1-2delta} subset Q,
    Q subset {x,y>=-delta, x+y<=1+2delta}.            (3)

For the first inclusion, T_inner+[-delta,delta]^2 subset T, and
h_Q>=h_T-delta||u||_1 in every support direction u. Thus the
support function of T_inner is at most h_Q. This proves inclusion
without assuming a vertexwise matching of Q and T.

Take the leftmost Q point on the line y=1/2, the bottommost Q
point on x=1/2, and the last Q point on the diagonal x=y. They
have the forms

    w_1=(theta_1,1/2), w_2=(1/2,theta_2),
    w_0=(1/2+theta_0,1/2+theta_0), |theta_i|<=delta. (4)

Choose an actual Q side containing each of these boundary points;
if the point is a vertex, choose either incident side. The three
retained halfplanes have equations

    x>=c_1+b_1 y,  y>=c_2+b_2 x,
    (1-k)x+(1+k)y<=1+2theta_0,                      (5)

where

    |b_1|,|b_2|,|k|<=8delta, |c_1|,|c_2|<=5delta. (6)

Indeed the inner triangle contains (delta,1/4),(delta,3/4).
The left support line can be oriented as x>=theta_1+b_1(y-1/2):
its x coefficient is nonzero because Q has interior points on
both sides of y=1/2, and it is positive because Q extends to the
right on that horizontal line. The two inner points then give
|b_1|<=4(delta-theta_1)<=8delta, and c_1=theta_1-b_1/2.
The bottom line is identical. For the top line, the inner points
(3/4-delta,1/4-delta) and its coordinate swap give
|k|<=4(delta+theta_0)<=8delta. The diagonal coefficient has the
stated orientation since Q contains points below w_0 on x=y.
The three normal directions in (5) are distinct by (6).

Let S be the intersection of (5). This is a bounded triangle
containing Q. To check boundedness directly, the first two
halfplanes form a translated cone with rays (1,b_2),(b_1,1).
The top functional is positive on both rays, by at least
1-16delta-64delta^2>0. Its halfplane therefore bounds the cone;
Q has interior, so the resulting triangle is nondegenerate.

Let its vertices a_0,a_1,a_2 correspond to 0,e_1,e_2. Directly
solving the two-by-two systems gives

    ||a_0||_infinity<=6delta,
    ||a_i-e_i||_infinity<=30delta, i=1,2.            (7)

For example a_0's coordinates have absolute value at most
(5delta+40delta^2)/(1-64delta^2)<=6delta. At a_1 the x denominator
differs from one by at most 17delta and the numerator by at most
8delta. Thus |x-1|<=25delta/(1-17delta)<=26delta and |y|<=14delta.
These prove the slightly relaxed constants in (7).

Write M=(a_1-a_0,a_2-a_0), and map S to T by Phi(x)=M^(-1)(x-a_0).
Every entry of M-I has absolute value at most 36delta, so
||M^(-1)||_infinity<=1/(1-72delta). Equations (4),(7) imply that
each Phi(w_i) is within

    43delta/(1-72delta)<=44delta                    (8)

of the corresponding edge midpoint of T. Each selected S side
contains a genuine positive-length Q side, not just an incidental
supporting point. That fact will control the two unused cuts.

## 2. Exact two-cut normalization, including overlap

The pentagon has five actual sides and (5) selects three of them.
Consequently Q equals S intersected with its two remaining
halfplanes. Let R_1,R_2 be the closed pieces of S removed by
those two halfplanes; including their boundaries does not affect
area. Each is a triangle at exactly ONE vertex of S.

For proof, an excluded halfplane that contained two S vertices
would contain the interior point Phi(w_i) on their connecting
edge, contradicting w_i in Q. Boundary-vertex cases give the
same contradiction unless the excluded piece has zero area.
The unused Q sides are active and distinct, so their removed
pieces have positive area. Thus each cut has one removed vertex
and strictly retained other vertices.

The two incident-edge fractions of every R_j are at most

    1/2+44delta<501/1000,                            (9)

because the actual retained Q points w_i lie between the removed
edge intervals and the other endpoint, and (8) locates them.
Also, from (3),(7),

    |Q|>=(1-4delta)^2/2,
    |S|<=(1+72delta+2592delta^2)/2,
    tau=1-|Q|/|S|<=81delta<=81/1000000<1/10000.     (10)

The determinant upper bound in (10) follows by expanding a matrix
whose entries differ from I by at most 36delta. The displayed
ratio bound is immediate from
(80delta+2576delta^2)/(1+72delta+2592delta^2)<=81delta.

Set t_j=|R_j|/|S|. The product of its two edge fractions is t_j,
and t_j<=tau because R_j is a subset of the actual missing union.
Thus at least one incident fraction is at most sqrt(tau)<1/100.
Call that edge the short edge and the other the long edge; either
choice is allowed if both are short.

If the removed vertices are different, R_1 and R_2 have disjoint
interiors. On their shared S edge, the retained actual Q side
has positive length, so the two removed edge fractions a,b obey
a+b<1. At a hypothetical common point with third barycentric
coordinate v, their inequalities would imply
lambda_1<=b(1-v), lambda_2<=a(1-v), contradicting
lambda_1+lambda_2=1-v. The endpoint v=1 is retained by both cuts.
Hence in this case tau=t_1+t_2.

If both cuts remove the same vertex, their interiors can overlap
substantially. We keep the exact union mass

    tau=t_1+t_2-|R_1 intersect R_2|/|S|.            (11)

In particular t_1+t_2<=2tau, but it need not be close to tau.
No disjointness or subtraction of an overlap Helly count is used.

## 3. Uniform partial-loss bounds for low-volume caps

Work in barycentrics of S. The all-direction elementary cap lemma
proved in candidate 39f4da3e2b2dd7eb,
Section 2, says the following. If |lambda_i(y)-1/3|<=1/10000 and
a through-y S cap has fraction at most Gamma+1/10000, it isolates
one vertex and has equation

    a_j lambda_j+a_k lambda_k<=1,
    29/20<a_j,a_k<31/20.                             (12)

That proof includes two-vertex caps and vertex-boundary directions.
It depends only on S and the candidate window, not on the number
of cuts subsequently removed from S.

Consider a removed triangle at vertex i with short neighbor j and
long neighbor k. Its short coordinate u=lambda_j is at most 1/100,
and its long coordinate v=lambda_k has maximum at most 501/1000.
Every low-volume vertex-j cap excludes this removed triangle,
since its left side is at least (29/20)(1-u)>1. A vertex-k cap
can meet it only where

    v>=1-1/a_i+(a_j/a_i-1)u
      >9/29-1/1550>309/1000.                        (13)

The fraction of the removed triangle above that last threshold
is at most

    (1-(309/1000)/(501/1000))^2
                     =(64/167)^2<3/20.             (14)

Thus the per-piece loss vector is: its full mass at its own
vertex, zero at its short neighbor, and at most 3/20 of its mass
at its long neighbor. This slight sharpening of the quadrilateral
partial-tail bound supplies room for overlap accounting.

Define simultaneous upper loss bounds L_i, normalized by |S|,
as follows. For different removed vertices, sum the two vectors
just described. Because the pieces are disjoint, their sum is

    sum_i L_i=(23/20)tau.

For the SAME removed vertex i, instead put L_i=tau, the mass of
the actual UNION. For each other vertex, sum only the 3t_j/20
charges whose corresponding triangle has that vertex as its
long neighbor. This remains an upper bound on every actual cap
loss, even if the partial pieces overlap. It gives

    sum_i L_i<=tau+(3/20)(t_1+t_2)<=13tau/10.        (15)

In both cases 0<=L_i<=tau. Counting the own-vertex union just
once in (15) is essential. Summing both entire triangle volumes
there would not prove the required strict inequality.

## 4. One actual candidate pays all three loss bounds

Let Lbar=(L_0+L_1+L_2)/3 and choose

    lambda_i(y)=1/3+(3/4)(Lbar-L_i).                (16)

The coordinates sum to one. Since |lambda_i(y)-1/3|<=3tau/4,
(10) puts them in the window of (12). They are all positive.
For each removed triangle, its short coordinate at y is much
larger than 1/100, so y is strictly outside both removed pieces.
It is therefore an actual point of int Q.

Every one-vertex cap through y in S has fraction at least
4lambda_j(y)lambda_k(y), by the exact two-variable AM-GM
argument. For a low-volume cap of type i, subtracting the actual
loss bound L_i and using (16) gives at least

    Gamma-Lbar+4(lambda_j(y)-1/3)(lambda_k(y)-1/3)
      >=Gamma-13tau/30-9tau^2/4.                   (17)

Every other through-y cap has S fraction greater than
Gamma+1/10000. Removing at most tau<=1/10000 leaves more than
Gamma, so it also satisfies (17). This treats ALL directions
of the same actual body Q. Containing caps can be tightened
parallel to themselves through y.

Normalizing (17) by 1-tau proves

    D(Q)-Gamma
       >=[tau/90-9tau^2/4]/(1-tau)>=tau/180.        (18)

The last subtraction has numerator tau(1-404tau)/180, positive
for tau<=1/10000. This proves the total missing-area assertion.

For nested normalized uniform bodies TV(mu_Q,mu_S)=tau, so cap
distance is at most tau. Each R_j is an actual halfspace trace
of S with zero Q area, so cap distance is at least max(t_1,t_2).
Since tau<=t_1+t_2, this is at least tau/2. Equations (1)-(2)
follow, and affine invariance returns to the original frame.

The proof selects three actual supporting SIDE lines rather than
requiring the two unselected vertices to lie over different
edges of a chosen inner triangle. This directly handles both
possible two-cut incidence types, including substantial overlap
when two cuts remove the same outer-triangle vertex. No extension
to three or more unused side cuts is inferred from (15).

## 5. Exact overlap calibration and verification

In the standard S, take two cuts at vertex 0 with edge fractions
(2/5,epsilon) and (1/2,9epsilon/10). Both constraints are active,
so the retained body is an actual pentagon for small epsilon>0.
The two cut lines meet at (1/7,9epsilon/14). Their normalized
areas and intersection are

    t_1=2epsilon/5, t_2=9epsilon/20,
    I=27epsilon/70, tau=13epsilon/28.

Thus (t_1+t_2)/tau=119/65. Summing both whole-piece loss vectors
would give (23/20)(t_1+t_2)/tau=2737/1300>4/3, too large for
the argument. Counting the own-vertex UNION once instead gives

    [tau+(3/20)(t_1+t_2)]/tau=1657/1300<13/10.

This is an actual overlap obstruction to the naive summation,
not a counterexample to stability. The body is Hausdorff-infinity
within epsilon of S: points in the removed union can be moved
up by at most epsilon while remaining in S to reach the body.

The standard-library verifier
../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_near_triangle_pentagon_union_stability.py passes 30 actual
pentagon profiles, 8640 rational all-direction sample caps, 12
same-vertex union checks, 100 normalization-constant cases, and
the exact overlap identities above. The proof, rather than the
finite cap samples, establishes the continuum of directions.

The separate subsequent note
candidate 94bf8f29da63e55b supplies
a new union-homothety argument that removes the restriction on
the number of cuts. That extension is not inferred from (15) alone.
